title: Initiate New Relationships by Finding a Common Connection
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article offers a practical technique for initiating cold relationships: leveraging a shared mutual connection to lower the guard of both parties. A common contact provides social proof, reduces uncertainty, and gives both people something natural to talk about right away. The piece walks through how to ask a mutual contact for an introduction, what to do if that contact is uncomfortable making it, and how to reference the shared connection early in the conversation to keep it as a launching pad for further rapport. It closes by advising the reader to follow up with the connector afterward as a courtesy.
points: Using a mutual connection to initiate a relationship reduces uncertainty and puts both parties at ease.
Social media has made it easier to discover previously unknown mutual connections.
When asking a mutual contact for an introduction, be prepared for hesitation and find another shared connection if needed.
Reference the shared connection early and throughout the conversation, and follow up with the connector afterward.
quotes: establishing a relationship through a “cold” one-way introduction is among the scariest and most difficult of human tasks.
Common connections put people at ease, offer social proof that the other party is safe to speak with
The good news is that social media now makes it easy to learn of mutual connections you had no idea existed.
The shared reference point is a great launching pad into other points of shared interest.
be sure to follow up with the person you reference. They will be pleased to know that the circle of relationships has been expanded.
